newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS V BORUSSIA DORTMUND HIGHLIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS V BORUSSIA DORTMUND HIGHLIGHTS.

text.p: Juventus manager Marcello Lippi named just five players who appeared in last year's European Cup final in the team attempting to retain the trophy against Borussia Dortmund at the Olympic Stadium on Wednesday.

The only survivors from the winning side 12 months ago were goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi, defender Ciro Ferrara and midfielder Didier Deschamps along with Angelo Di Livio and Vladimir Jugovic who both came on as substitutes in last year's final.

Paulo Sousa, who played in last year's Juventus team, was in the Dortmund lineup against his former club. Three other Dortmund players -- Stefan Reuter, Andreas Moeller and Juergen Kohler are also former Juve players.

Dortmund manager Ottmar Hitzfeld, who has used 24 players during his team's route to their first European Cup final, left out Rene Tretschok and Lars Ricken, the players whose goals secured a 2-0 aggregate win over Manchester United in the semifinals, from the starting lineup.
European Player of the Year Matthias Sammer returned as libero with Portugese midfielder Paulo Sousa returning in midfield.

The Olympic Stadium was bathed in evening sunlight at the kickoff of a match being watched in a record number of 202 countries and territories around the world with an estimated global audience of 500 million.

Both defences were put under early pressure with Dortmund fortunate to survive appeals for a penalty after only three minutes when Stefan Reuter appeared to bring down Vladimir Jugovic in the area. Hungarian referee Sandor Puhl, close to the incident, waved play on.
Both teams won corners in the opening exchanges and Mark Juliano had an opportunity to score from Zinedine Zidane's fourth minute corner but fluffed his header from eight metres.
Christian Vieri shot into the side netting with only goalkeeper Stefan Klos to beat after six minutes for the first clearcut chance of the game.
Juventus, wearing their change kit of all blue, got into their stride sooner than Dortmund and Zidane was forcing Juventus's pressing game, giving Dortmund no time to settle.
On the few occasions Dortmund attempted to counter, the Juve defence quickly reacted to any danger.

Juventus's shaven-headed defender Sergio Porrini became the first player to be shown a yellow card after 20 minutes for a badly timed lunge on Stephane Chapuisat who was thwarted in trying to set up another Dortmund attack.
Three minutes later Sousa was booked for a trip on his former team mate Didier Deschamps but Deschamps was then positioned too far wide at Zidane's free kick to make anything of the chance.
